title: SLO mapping for feature flags and canary capacity handbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose
This handbook defines how Service Level Objectives (SLOs), error budgets, and capacity planning interact with feature-flagged rollouts and canary campaigns at Redwood Inference. It is intended for SREs, release engineers, and product/feature owners who run progressive rollouts on the hosted and dedicated surfaces.

Scope
- Applies to any deployment that uses: (a) feature-flag traffic splits, (b) canary routing, or (c) staged model/quantization rollouts.
- Covers SLO mapping, canary capacity sizing, telemetry requirements, incident triggers tied to feature flags, and postmortem evidence expectations.

Why this matters
Progressive rollouts reduce blast radius but create complex cross-cutting reliability requirements: canaries should not silently burn error budgets or consume reserved capacity without explicit mapping to SLOs and escape hatches. This doc ensures consistent decisions, automation hooks, and clear evidence for incident reviews.

Key concepts and definitions
- SLI (Service Level Indicator): a telemetry metric (e.g., generation latency P95/P99, 5xx rate, token throughput) used to compute an SLO.
- SLO: stated goal for an SLI (e.g., "generation P95 < 250ms, availability >= 99.9% per month").
- Error budget: 1 - SLO; tracked on per-service and per-tenant basis.
- Canary: a small, controlled traffic cohort routed to a new model, runtime, or feature flag version.
- Feature flag rollout: a staged increase in flag-enabled traffic weight controlled by the release system.

High-level policy (TL;DR)
- Every canary/feature flag that affects inference path must have an SLO mapping document linked in the PR.
- Initial canary traffic <= 5% of global traffic unless explicit exemption approved by SRE lead.
- Canary must reserve a minimum of 3x SLA headroom in tokens/s or GPU slots to avoid cross-tenant interference during warm-up.
- If a canary consumes >25% of the service-level error budget in a 24h window, automatic rollback is triggered.

SLO mapping workflow (step-by-step)
1) Pre-rollout: Create or update the "SLO mapping" section in the feature PR and include: owner, affected services, SLIs, expected traffic profile, token/sec estimate, and required headroom. Use the template below.
2) Canary sizing: SREs compute required capacity: baseline utilization + canary delta + 3x warmup cushion. Verify on the capacity dashboard.
3) Canary run: Start at configured initial weight. Monitor SLI dashboards and the canary evidence channel.
4) Decision gates: Evaluate the canary at each stage against automated checks (below). If a gate fails, invoke rollback or throttle.
5) Post-rollout: Produce a short reconciliation note linking the canary evidence and any SLO/error-budget changes.

Automated gates and thresholds
- Gate A: Latency gate — P95 increase vs baseline <= 15% AND absolute P95 <= configured SLO margin (e.g., 1.15 * SLO P95).
- Gate B: Error rate gate — 5xx-related errors attributable to canary <= 0.05% absolute increase OR <= 10% relative increase to baseline error rate, whichever is smaller.
- Gate C: Error budget gate — canary must not burn >25% of the monthly error budget in any continuous 24h window.
- Gate D: Capacity gate — canary CPU/GPU utilization increase must leave >= 20% cluster spare capacity for emergency bursts.

Canary sizing calculation (example)
- Baseline tokens/sec: 80k tokens/s
- Expected canary traffic: 3% of baseline = 2.4k tokens/s
- Average token cost per second (inferred): 0.00012 GPU-slot per token/s
- Required additional GPU-slots = 2.4k * 0.00012 = 0.288 -> round to 1 slot (minimum allocation rules)
- Warm-up cushion: 3x -> allocate 3 slots for canary
- Final reserved slots: max(1, 3) = 3 slots

Template: SLO mapping snippet (to include in PR)
```
SLO mapping:
- owner: <team-or-person>
- service: rdx-generation-api
- slis: [generation_p95_ms, tokens_per_sec, 5xx_rate]
- target_slos: {generation_p95_ms: "< 250ms (monthly)", availability: ">= 99.9%"}
- initial_canary_weight: 0.03
- expected_tokens_s: 2400
- reserved_gpu_slots: 3
- rollback_criteria: ["P95 increase > 15%", "5xx delta > 0.05%", "error_budget_burn_24h > 25%"]
```

Operational tooling and dashboarding requirements
- Every canary must feed a dedicated telemetry group tagged with: env, canary_id, flag, model_version, cluster_id. This allows rapid attribution.
- Dashboard widgets to create before rollout:
  - Canary vs baseline latency (P50/P95/P99) with delta shading.
  - Error budget burn rate chart (per-hour and 24h rolling).
  - Capacity utilization: GPU slots by cluster, token/sec, OOM/GC events.
  - Canary traffic split and percentage timeline.
- Alerts (on-call triggers):
  - Canary-latency-high: P95_canary > 1.15 * SLO_P95 for 3 consecutive 1-minute buckets -> page.
  - Canary-5xx-spike: 5xx_delta > 0.05% sustained for 5 minutes -> page.
  - Canary-errorbudget-surge: projected 24h burn rate > 25% of monthly budget -> page + auto-throttle.

Runbook: immediate actions when a canary page fires
1) Acknowledge and assign owner. Post short hypothesis in the incident channel.
2) Switch canary routing to hold or reduce weight: run loaderctl canary set-weight --id <id> --weight <new_weight> (recommended < 1%).
3) Snapshot telemetry: run rdx-observe export --canary <id> --window 15m --out /tmp/canary_snapshot.json and attach to the incident.
4) If 5xx spike or OOMs appear, toggle the feature flag to off (kill-switch): ffctl toggle --flag <flag> --state off --reason "canary_failure".
5) If capacity-related, scale additional GPU-slots via autoscale API (fast-path): rdx-scale cluster <cluster> --add-slots 2 --reason "canary warmup".
6) If error budget is burning too fast, trigger automated rollback: rdx-release rollback --canary <id> --immediate.
7) Notify product and stake-holders with annotated snapshot and initial mitigations.

Incident review and evidence standard for canary-related incidents
Every canary incident must follow the incident review template below. Reviews should be completed within 7 business days of triage. At minimum include:
- Title and incident id
- Summary (what changed, who started the canary, traffic percentages, duration)
- SLIs impacted and pre/post windows (show P50/P95/P99, error rates, tokens/sec)
- Error budget impact (per-tenant and service-level) with a quantitative estimate (see example calculation)
- Causation hypothesis and tests run (link to experiment logs)
- Action items (short-term fixes, long-term mitigations), owners, and due dates
- Attachments: canary snapshot JSON, router event logs (first 30 minutes), stack traces, and feature flag audit trail

Example incident evidence checklist (copy into postmortem)
| Evidence item | Required? | Location / CLI |
|---|---:|---|
| Canary telemetry snapshot | Yes | /incidents/<id>/canary_snapshot.json |
| Router weight timeline | Yes | router-events --canary <id> --range 00:30 |
| Error budget burn chart | Yes | slo-dashboard -> export PNG |
| Stack traces / OOM logs | Conditional | cloud-logs query: service="rdx" AND canary_id=<id> |
| FF audit trail | Yes | ff-service audit --id <flag-id> |

Capacity planning considerations for multi-tenant clusters
- Conservative reserve: always maintain a contingency pool equal to the 99th percentile of historical microburst demand for the last 30 days, or 15% of cluster capacity, whichever is larger.
- Soft preemption: canaries should be placed in soft-preemptible pools when possible. The preemption policy must be documented in the PR and the SRE-runbook.
- Tenant isolation: ensure headroom is allocated per-tenant in the allocation ledger (see ledger example below). Under no circumstances should a single canary permanently consume more than 10% of global reserved capacity.

Allocation ledger (table format)
| tenant | reserved_slots | ephemeral_canary_slots | last_updated |
| acme-corp | 10 | 2 | 2026-02-10 |
| internal-evals | 6 | 3 | 2026-02-12 |
| free-tier | 2 | 0 | 2025-11-01 |

Escalation matrix (who to call)
1) Canary owner (first line)
2) SRE on-call for the affected cluster (page)
3) Runtime-team lead (if capacity actions or kernel-level issues suspected)
4) Product owner and release manager (if rollback or customer impact)

Post-canary checklist (must be completed within 48h of 100% rollout)
- Confirm all canary SLIs returned to baseline or improved.
- Reconcile token/sec billing estimates with capacity usage.
- Update SLO projections if the new variant meaningfully changes cost/latency profiles (PR to slo-config repo).
- Archive canary telemetry under /canary-archives/<id>/ with standardized metadata.

Examples: two realistic scenarios
1) Latency bump but no errors: P95 jumps from 180ms -> 260ms for canary at 5% traffic. Action: reduce to 1%, run localized perf trace, compare kernel scheduling traces; if root cause is model quantization, either tune config or rollback.
2) Error budget burn: canary causes 0.12% absolute increase in 5xx for a tenant with 0.3% monthly budget. At current burn rate, this projects to 40% monthly burn. Action: immediate rollback and incident review with evidence snapshot.

Related pages and templates
- SLO configuration repository: /confluence/eng-sre/capacity-planning/slo-configs (link)
- Canary telemetry tagging standards: /confluence/eng-sre/operational-tooling/canary-tagging-guidelines (link)
- Feature flag emergency toggle runbook: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/feature-flag-kill-switch (link)

Owners and maintenance
- Primary owner: SRE Release Safety (team) — contact: s-releasesafety@redwood.ai
- Maintenance cadence: review annually or after any canary incident with >25% error budget impact.

Appendix: useful CLI snippets
- Set canary weight:
  loaderctl canary set-weight --id cny-2026-021 --weight 0.01 --reason "emergency_hold"
- Export telemetry snapshot:
  rdx-observe export --canary cny-2026-021 --window 15m --out ./cny-2026-021-snapshot.json
- Toggle feature flag (kill-switch):
  ffctl toggle --flag rdx.experimental.new-kv-cache --state off --reason "canary_failure"
